key_insight: Lamination solves packaging of foil arrays: modest 8-32-sheet edge-plated stacks (3D-Plus style) could package I-01819 foil dies into module-sized parts.
killer_doubt: Stacking leaves $/bit unchanged and HBM already reaches ~300-400 GB/cm3; 800 laminations at 99.9% yield each give 45%; PI at 0.12 W/mK gives ~800 K/W through 1 cm.
decisive_experiment: Laminate 32 test foils (daisy chains plus TFT monitors) with ACF and edge plating (~$150k); measure per-interface yield, contact resistance and in-stack thermal resistance before building any memory.
prior_art: Irvine Sensors and 3D-Plus edge-plated laminated die stacks; HBM and 3D NAND already exceed the claimed volumetric density.

key_insight: Transistor-written IGZO gain cell passes the endurance wall; DRAM cost parity is ~$440/m2 at 300 GB/m2, and one 1 m R2R line (~5e6 m2/yr) could make ~1.5 EB/yr.
killer_doubt: Multilevel 100 nm overlay on foil: PI moves 10-20 ppm/K plus humidity, and 10 ppm over 1 cm is 100 nm; realistic $150-300/m2 gives ~$0.5-1/GB, not $0.1.
decisive_experiment: SAIL-style single multilevel stamp on PI-on-glass or steel foil (~$400k, university NIL tool): 1 Mb IGZO 2T gain-cell array at 100-200 nm; map overlay, killer defects/cm2, Vt sigma, retention at 85 C.
prior_art: HP Labs SAIL R2R oxide TFTs, ~15 cm2/Vs (via search snippet); PragmatIC FlexIC/FlexRV IGZO at ~0.6-0.8 um. Sub-micron R2R oxide memory array: none found.

key_insight: Domain-wall shifting has no charge-fluence wear, so it is one of the four endurance-safe write routes; 64 bits per track could beat 1b density ~10x.
killer_doubt: Head fabs build ~1e4-1e5 readers per AlTiC wafer with no CMOS and no HAR verticals; racetrack needs ~1e10 tracks/cm2 with shift errors below 1e-12 per shift, never shown.
decisive_experiment: Fold into N-82: electroplate 20 nm Co/Ni wires in an AAO or Si mold, write 16 domains, shift 1e9 times, and count shift errors by MFM/TMR readback (~$300k).
prior_art: IBM/Parkin racetrack since 2008, stalled on pinning; Phase B N-82 capacitor-hole racetrack covers the same physics with a better fab route.

key_insight: Bind the certificate to the module's DRAM retention-failure map, a physical unclonable fingerprint, instead of the rewritable SPD serial, so certificates cannot move to counterfeits.
killer_doubt: A $300 FPGA tops out near DDR4-2400, so DDR5-4800+ speed bins need ~$5k+ parts; VRT cells make one-shot retention maps drift; the certificate price premium is unproven.
decisive_experiment: Test 500 used DDR4 modules on DRAM Bender/SoftMC (~$100k): repeat retention maps over 30 days to measure fingerprint stability and VRT churn; sell 200 certified vs uncertified lots and compare prices.
prior_art: ETH SAFARI SoftMC/DRAM Bender open FPGA testers; CST and RAMCHECK commercial testers; Blancco-style signed ITAD certificates; academic DRAM retention PUFs.

key_insight: Server-side defaults (JVM heap, Kubernetes requests running 2-3x over use) map directly to purchased DRAM; client resident memory does not.
killer_doubt: $1M is tiny beside Chromium's existing memory teams (PartitionAlloc, Memory Saver); devices ship RAM in fixed tiers, so a 10% RSS cut moves ~0% of bits shipped.
decisive_experiment: Measure the server case instead: audit requested vs resident memory for 1,000 Kubernetes pods at three cloud tenants (~$100k) and price the DRAM a right-sizing nudge would free.
prior_art: Chromium PartitionAlloc and Memory Saver tab discarding; Electron footprint work; Google Patch Rewards; Kubernetes VPA right-sizing tools.

key_insight: A buyer-only index (hyperscalers, OEMs, distributors) aligns incentives: buyers gain from deflating phantom demand, sellers need not join, and MPC lowers the antitrust exposure of sharing.
killer_doubt: Three makers (~95% share) gain from spikes and carry price-fixing history (2002-06 fines), so they won't join; spikes mostly reflect inelastic demand and 3-5-year fab lead times.
decisive_experiment: Run a 6-month MPC pilot with 10-15 buyers (~$500k): weekly aggregate inventory-weeks and order indices; test whether it predicts contract-price turns and cuts double-ordering against TrendForce baselines.
prior_art: JODI oil data; WSTS monthly aggregates; TrendForce/DRAMeXchange inventory estimates; Boston Women's Workforce Council MPC wage-gap study.

key_insight: Zero-hardware delivery runs at native platform speed, so speed-bin and pattern tests are real; it is the software half of I-08260.
killer_doubt: Most stock hosts cannot stretch or disable refresh, so the 8-hour 'retention' test only checks the 64 ms spec; the SPD serial is rewritable, so the signature is forgeable.
decisive_experiment: Not worth separate funding; fold into I-08260. Quick check: on 100 modules, compare MemTest86 Pro results at stock vs BIOS tREFI raised 4x to see whether retention outliers appear.
prior_art: MemTest86 Pro per-module reports with SPD data; ITAD certification practice (R2v3, e-Stewards, Blancco). Adding a signature contributes little.

key_insight: Serving many personal models from one resident base is the right shape; delta size, not base size, decides memory per user.
killer_doubt: BitDelta already does exactly this; a rank-16 LoRA on a 7B model costs ~0.04-0.1 bit per base weight, 10-25x below a 1-bit delta, and S-LoRA/Punica serve thousands.
decisive_experiment: None needed; existing BitDelta and S-LoRA results settle it. If pursued, compare BitDelta vs LoRA-16 storage and quality for 1,000 user fine-tunes on one GPU (<$20k).
prior_art: BitDelta (Liu et al., 2024): sign-only deltas with per-matrix scales and a multi-tenant kernel; S-LoRA and Punica multi-adapter serving.

key_insight: Attention mass concentrates on sinks and recent tokens, so mixed precision beats eviction; ~3-4 bits average is a real 4-5x KV cut.
killer_doubt: Published many times (KIVI, MiKV, ZipCache, H2O, StreamingLLM); past attention mass misses query-dependent retrieval, so demoted needles lose accuracy at INT2.
decisive_experiment: Nothing beyond the literature is needed; if pursued, run RULER/needle tests at 128k on an open model comparing the age ladder with MiKV/ZipCache at equal bits (<$20k GPU time).
prior_art: KIVI 2-bit KV; MiKV importance-aware mixed precision; ZipCache salient-token quantization; H2O heavy-hitter eviction; StreamingLLM attention sinks.

key_insight: Phone DRAM is sized partly for warm apps; forcing small, re-creatable state would decouple perceived warmth from resident heap.
killer_doubt: Android saved-instance state, the low-memory killer, the cached-app freezer and zRAM already do this; on-device LLMs (Apple Intelligence needs 8 GB) now set phone RAM.
decisive_experiment: Profile 50 popular apps on 6 GB vs 12 GB Android phones (~$50k): measure relaunch time and state loss after forced process death, and whether OEM RAM tiers could shift.
prior_art: Android saved-instance state and process-death restore; iOS state restoration; Android cached-app freezer; zRAM swap.

key_insight: ZFP fixed-rate mode yields fixed-size blocks, so a CXL expander can compress lossily at line rate without the indirection tables that burden variable-size compressed memory.
killer_doubt: ML stacks already quantize activations and KV to FP8/INT4 in software; 3-8x on 30-60% of the footprint is only 1.25-2.1x overall.
decisive_experiment: FPGA CXL Type-3 card with fixed-rate ZFP (~$300k): run HPC fields, analytics sketches and FP8 activations through an mmap lossy region; measure effective capacity, added latency and end-task error.
prior_art: AVR in-controller approximate compression (Chalmers, 2019); Flikker; EnerJ; ZeroPoint lossless memory-compression IP; ZFP/SZ hardware cores.

key_insight: Bandwidth per GB, not FLOPS, sets KV-serving value: V100 (~28/s) and A100-80 (~25/s) scan their HBM nearly as often as H100 (~42/s), at similar or lower W/GB.
killer_doubt: Each token needs ~80 per-layer round trips (~1-2 ms) and ~20 GB/s per H100 at batch 256; V100 lacks BF16/FlashAttention-2; the retired HBM2 pool is likely only tens of PB.
decisive_experiment: Rack 8 used V100 or A100 servers as attention/KV nodes behind 2 H100 nodes over 400G RDMA (~$300k); serve a 70B GQA model at 32-128k context; measure tok/s/$ against H100-only.
prior_art: Lamina attention offloading to cheaper memory-optimized GPUs (2024); MegaScale-Infer and StepFun attention-FFN disaggregation (2025). Retired-fleet sourcing angle: none found.
